title: Middle East Airlines 438
summary: Middle East Airlines Flight 438, a Boeing 720 with 81 aboard, was destroyed by a bomb in flight at 11,300 feet on January 1, 1976, while en route from Beirut to Dubai via Abu Dhabi. The bomb was planted in the cargo hold by Omani militants with a timer set to explode after landing in Muscat. Flight delays from boarding and baggage loading caused the bomb to detonate in flight. The aircraft broke up and crashed 37 kilometers northwest of Qaisumah, Saudi Arabia.
probable_cause: An explosive device was detonated in the aircraft cargo hold by Omani militants during cruise flight, causing structural failure and in-flight breakup.

factors.evidence: Bomb was planted on board by Omani militants with timer set to explode after landing at Muscat airport but exploded early while aircraft was still cruising due to flight delays.
Bomb was able to be planted in cargo hold; inadequate security screening and cargo handling procedures allowed the device to reach the aircraft.
Aircraft broke up at altitude of 11,300 meters as result of bomb explosion in cargo hold.

events.text: Flight 438 departed Beirut; bomb planted in cargo hold by Omani militants with timer set to explode after landing at Muscat.
At 05:30, one hour and forty minutes after departure at 11300 feet altitude, bomb exploded in front section of cargo hold.
Aircraft broke up at altitude of 11,300 meters and crashed 37 kilometers northwest of Qaisumah, Saudi Arabia.

title: Aeroflot 3739 (1976)
summary: Aeroflot Flight 3739, a Tupolev Tu-104A, crashed during takeoff from Irkutsk on February 9, 1976. The aircraft began rolling to the right at 300 km/h rotation speed, forcing pilots to roll it 20 degrees left. Calculations showed the right fuel tanks held 1,300-1,500 kg more fuel than the left, creating asymmetric weight. The pilots' aileron inputs were inadequate; the proper response would have been to reduce throttle sharply. The aircraft became uncontrollable at 30 m altitude and crashed 180 m past the runway end at a 70° bank angle, killing 24 of 114 aboard.
probable_cause: Asymmetric refueling with right fuel tanks holding 1,300-1,500 kg more fuel than left combined with inadequate pilot response in adjusting ailerons instead of reducing throttle during rotation.

title: Aeroflot 909
summary: An Ilyushin Il-18E at flight level 260 experienced an electrical failure that disabled critical flight instruments including the compass and both main gyros. It was dark and the aircraft was in clouds with no natural horizon. The crew became confused about aircraft orientation and lost control. The aircraft crashed near Voronezh killing all 111 aboard, including 7 people on the ground, making it the deadliest aviation accident in Soviet Russia.

title: Aeroflot 1802
summary: Aeroflot Flight 1802, an Antonov An-24RV, crashed near Chernigovskiy airport after the rudder suddenly deflected while descending through 5700 meters. The rudder deflected 25 degrees to the right, changing roll and yaw angles, causing severe disturbances. Propellers were feathered and the aircraft entered a tailspin, impacting the ground in uncontrolled descent.
probable_cause: Loss of control caused by the rudder deflecting when the autopilot was disconnected. The root cause of the rudder deflection was never determined; possible causes include accidental rudder trim control or electrical failure.

factors.evidence: The airliner reached sharp angles of attack, and thus went into a tailspin and crashed in uncontrolled flight.

events.text: Flight 1802 was flying at an altitude of 5700 meters with a speed of 350 km/h.

title: Air Manila 702
summary: Air Manila Flight 702, a Lockheed L-188A Electra with 33 passengers and 12 crew, crashed during takeoff from runway 6L at Naval Air Station Agana on 4 June 1976. Seconds after lifting off, engine number three propeller feathered. The captain continued the takeoff despite not yet reaching VR speed, when company policy and safety procedures required immediate abort. The aircraft reached only 75-100 feet altitude before crashing into terrain beyond the runway.
probable_cause: The primary cause was the flight crew's inappropriate response to the engine failure; the captain continued flight with the engine failure despite safely being able to abort takeoff before reaching VR speed.

title: 1976 Sabah Air GAF Nomad crash

At 600 feet altitude approaching the runway at 86 knots, the aircraft stalled with one wing dipping down and spiraled into shallow water. The aircraft broke in two with all 11 on board killed, including the Chief Minister of Sabah and other senior political figures. The investigation determined pilot error was the cause.

title: ČSA 001
summary: A Czechoslovak Airlines Ilyushin Il-18B crashed into Zlaté Piesky Lake on final approach to Bratislava on 28 July 1976, killing 76 of the 79 people on board. The crew executed a highly unstabilized ILS approach with excessive descent rates of 4,320 feet per minute instead of the normal 10 meters per second, variable speeds, and improper flap configuration changes. The crew inadvertently set thrust reversal on the inboard engines while still airborne, causing engine number 3 to fail and feathering engine number 4, resulting in loss of control and impact with the lake.
probable_cause: Crew error during approach involving improper execution of a highly unstabilized approach profile, including inadvertent thrust reversal at altitude, erroneous engine feathering, and failure to recover during the attempted go-around.

factors.evidence: The crew executed a highly unstabilized ILS instrument approach with rates of descent as high as 4,320 feet per minute.

The crew then inadvertently feathered the no. 4 prop, losing all thrust on the right side of the aircraft.
The right bank due to asymmetric thrust increased and the aircraft lost control at 40 meters altitude.
The aircraft struck lake Zlaté Piesky in a 60 degree right bank and a 60 degree nose down attitude.

title: SAETA 232
summary: A SAETA Vickers Viscount carrying 55 passengers and four crew members departed Quito for Cuenca on 15 August 1976. The pilot's last contact occurred over Ambato during cruise at high altitude. The aircraft crashed on Chimborazo volcano at 5,310 meters, where the wreckage remained hidden below the glacier for 27 years. No formal investigation was conducted. The cause remains unknown.
probable_cause: The cause of the accident is not known. No investigation was conducted as the accident site was declared a graveyard.

title: 1976 Zagreb mid-air collision

aircraft.type: Hawker Siddeley Trident and Douglas DC-9-32

summary: British Airways Flight 476 (Hawker Siddeley Trident) and Inex-Adria Flight 550 (Douglas DC-9) collided mid-air near Zagreb VOR. The middle-sector controller requested upper-sector controller approval for the DC-9 to climb to flight level 350. The upper-sector controller approved the climb, believing he was watching the correct target climb past an aircraft descending through the same area. Both aircraft were at the same altitude at the collision point. The accident resulted from a procedural error by air traffic controllers in Zagreb.
probable_cause: A procedural error by air traffic controllers in Zagreb, specifically the failure of the upper-sector controller to prevent the climb clearance when an aircraft was descending through the requested flight level.

title: Turkish Airlines 452
summary: Turkish Airlines Flight 452 crashed into Karatepe Hill near Isparta after the first officer mistook city lights of Isparta for the runway at Antalya. The pilots attempted visual flight at night instead of using instruments, mistaking dark mountains for the Mediterranean Sea. The aircraft descended too early and crashed into a hill.
probable_cause: Pilot error: the first officer mistook the city lights of Isparta for the runway of Antalya and the aircraft descended too early. The pilots attempted visual flight instead of required instrumental flight at night.

title: Cubana 455
summary: Eleven minutes after takeoff from Barbados at 18,000 feet, two bombs detonated on board planted by Cuban exile terrorist group CORU. One bomb in the rear lavatory destroyed control cables, while another in the passenger cabin created a hole and started a fire. The aircraft entered a rapid uncontrolled descent and crashed 8 km offshore. All 73 on board died, including all 24 members of the Cuban national fencing team.

title: Indian Airlines 171
summary: Indian Airlines Flight 171 suffered an uncontained engine failure of the No. 2 engine shortly after takeoff from Bombay Airport. Metal fatigue in the 10th stage high-pressure compressor disk caused it to disintegrate, with fragments severing fuel lines. Fuel leaked into the engine and ignited, producing an uncontrolled fire that consumed the aircraft's hydraulic fluid. The crew attempted an emergency landing but the aircraft lost control at 300 feet altitude and crashed 1000 yards from the runway end.
probable_cause: Metal fatigue in the 10th stage compressor disk caused an uncontained engine failure with resulting loss of hydraulic fluid due to fire in the engine bay. The crew was unable to recover control of the aircraft and it crashed during the emergency landing approach.

title: Olympic Airways 830
summary: Olympic Airways Flight 830, a NAMC YS-11 turboprop, unable to land at Larissa due to bad weather, diverted to Kozani at 5500 ft. The aircraft flew into a mountain at 4625 ft near Servia in cloud conditions with no visual references, killing all 50 on board. The aircraft was on a heading of 310 degrees when it first struck the ground and disintegrated over 200 meters.

title: EgyptAir 864
summary: EgyptAir Flight 864, a Boeing 707, crashed into a weaving mill in Bangkok at 03:45 local time while approaching Runway 21L. All 52 on board were killed. The investigation found pilot error in descending below minimum altitude without proper monitoring, combined with inadequate weather information from ATC regarding visibility of only 4,000 m with low clouds.
